newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares advance, seen steady.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares advance, seen steady.

text.p: Austrian shares ended ahead on Wednesday after a tentative start with the benchmark index buoyed by across-the-board buying of blue chips, notably VA Stahl and Flughafen.
Traders see the market trading with a steady tone on Thursday, the last day of trade before the Easter holidays, but see the ATX index capped at 1,230 points.
"As long as we haven't overcome 1,230, there're going to be no big leaps ahead. And I don't see that happening tomorrow," said one trader.
The ATX gained 0.66 percent to 1,223.48 after earlier slipping to 1,212.99. Of its 21 constituents, 15 advanced while six fell.
The top gainer was microchip maker AMS, recovering another 29 schillings to 1,100 after suffering recent heavy selling.

Another strong performer was fireproof materials maker Radex-Heraklith, up 8.9 schillings to 447.9, after reporting 1996 group net profit rose 24.6 percent to 582 million schillings and that it expected further earnings growth in 1997.
Radex earlier hit a new high for the year at 450 schillings.
The day's worst performer was beverage group BBAG, falling 10 schillings to 755.
The all-share Vienna bourse index climbed 0.47 percent to 458.58.
In the futures market, the April ATX contract rose 11 points to 1,228.5 on turnover of 743.
